messages:
maria_support: Customer on macOS (Python 3.11 / M1) reports ImportError after pip installing redwood-sdk[speed] — error:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/bin/app.py", line 2, in <module>
    from redwood import RedwoodClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx' (/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/__init__.py)

maria_support: Repro steps the customer provided: pip install redwood-sdk[speed]==1.4.3, then python -c "from redwood import RedwoodClient" fails. They say it started after a system pip upgrade this morning.

dylan_eng: ugh, looks like an httpx API change — which httpx ended up installed? can you get `pip show httpx` and `pip show redwood-sdk` from them?

maria_support: asked for pip show outputs, they sent back:
```
Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 1.4.3
---
Name: httpx
Version: 0.24.0
```

katie_docs: I think redwood-sdk[speed] extras still import AsyncClient from httpx 0.23.*, and httpx 0.24 renamed/moved some symbols. We changed the extras in 1.4.4 to adapt but 1.4.3 still expects older httpx. quick workaround: `pip install 'httpx<0.24'` or upgrade to SDK 1.4.4 if available.

maria_support: customer tried `pip install httpx==0.23.3` and reports import now works. They said they can't upgrade to 1.4.4 because their CI pins exact SDK version due to enterprise policy.

dylan_eng: okay, for a short-term fix we can recommend pinning httpx<0.24 in their requirements. For a longer-term fix we should backport a patch to 1.4.3 extras so it doesn't pull httpx 0.24 when users `pip install redwood-sdk[speed]`. I'll open an eng issue.

katie_docs: also adding an explicit note in install docs: "If you use extras `[speed]` and are on older lockfiles/CI pins, pin httpx<0.24 or upgrade redwood-sdk to >=1.4.4." saves people the back-and-forth.

maria_support: customer asked whether this could cause runtime 401s they saw earlier — they saw ImportError on start, then after workaround the client sometimes raises 401 with identical env. any ideas?

dylan_eng: separate thing: httpx version mismatch could change headers behavior only slightly but 401s are typically auth/token related. Ask them to `repr(client._session.headers)` or share the auth header they set (redact token). Also check they didn't have an older cached package where client code expected different default scopes.

maria_support: asked customer to run `python -c "import httpx, redwood; print(httpx.__version__, redwood.__version__)"` and to share a redacted `requests` log. their last reply: `0.23.3 1.4.3` and redacted log shows `401 Authorization failed for /v1/generate` immediately after the initial connection.

dylan_eng: sounds like a real auth token issue. checklist: 1) confirm env var name expected by SDK (REDWOOD_API_KEY) 2) ensure no trailing whitespace/newline in token 3) confirm account not suspended/billing issue 4) if using private/dedicated, confirm route/model mapping. I'll run a quick token parity check from our side if they share masked token.

maria_support: customer provided masked token and we confirmed it matches server record but their account had an overdue invoice flagged yesterday — accounting has auto-suspended API keys until billing is cleared. escalated to finance.

maria_support: summary/workaround posted to customer: 1) pin httpx<0.24 for existing SDK 1.4.3 installs (temporary) 2) if possible upgrade to redwood-sdk>=1.4.4 which bundles compatibility fixes 3) 401s were due to billing suspension; clearing invoice restored keys.

dylan_eng: created ENG-4201 to backport a setup.py extras constraint and add a test that `pip install redwood-sdk[speed]` resolves httpx<0.24 for 1.4.3 users, and also added a CI job to smoke test imports on macOS/ARM.

katie_docs: I'll open a small docs PR to call out the httpx pin and add a troubleshooting blurb under "Install & Imports".

deploy-bot: [deploy] patch/eng-4201 queued for CI — 3 tests running :hourglass_flowing_sand:
